sections.body:
### Exercise 1 — Max Retry Count
Modify the invoice parser so that after 3 retries the agent stops trying and returns `needs_human_review=True` with whatever it has, instead of raising `UsageLimitExceeded`.

### Exercise 2 — Date Range Validator
Add a `@field_validator` on `invoice_date` that rejects dates more than 30 days in the past (with `ModelRetry`). Test by feeding the agent a 2022 invoice date.

### Exercise 3 — Add a Second MCP Server
Connect both the filesystem MCP server and the SQLite MCP server (`mcp-server-sqlite --db-path /tmp/test.db`) to one agent. Ask the agent to "create a table called notes with one column content, then insert the contents of /tmp/hello.txt into it, then read it back."

<details>
<summary>Solution 1</summary>

```python
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelRetry, UsageLimitExceeded
from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits

@invoice_agent.result_validator
def validate_invoice(result: Invoice) -> Invoice:
    try:
        # The validator body runs inside a try so we can detect repeated failure
        if result.invoice_date > date.today():
            raise ModelRetry("Date is in the future; re-extract.")
    except ModelRetry:
        # On the last allowed retry, mark for human review instead of looping
        result.needs_human_review = True
    return result

async def safe_run(text: str) -> Invoice:
    try:
        result = await invoice_agent.run(text, usage_limit=3)
        return result.data
    except UsageLimitExceeded:
        # Fallback: ask once more with a "just mark for review" instruction
        forced = await invoice_agent.run(
            text + "\n\nIf you cannot parse this, set needs_human_review=True.",
            usage_limit=1,
        )
        forced.data.needs_human_review = True
        return forced.data
```

The key trick: catch `UsageLimitExceeded` and fall back to a single-shot run with an explicit instruction to set the flag.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Solution 2</summary>

```python
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pydantic import field_validator
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelRetry

class Invoice(BaseModel):
    vendor: str
    invoice_date: date
    total_usd: float
    needs_human_review: bool = False

    @field_validator("invoice_date")
    @classmethod
    def not_too_old(cls, v: date) -> date:
        cutoff = date.today() - timedelta(days=30)
        if v < cutoff:
            raise ModelRetry(
                f"invoice_date {v} is more than 30 days old ({cutoff} cutoff). "
                "Re-read the invoice; if the date really is that old, "
                "tell me explicitly."
            )
        return v

# Test
async def test_old_date():
    raw = "Vendor: Acme\nDate: 2022-01-01\nTotal: $100"
    result = await invoice_agent.run(raw, usage_limit=3)
    print(result.data)
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Solution 3</summary>

```python
# fs_and_sqlite_agent.py
import asyncio
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.mcp import MCPServerStdio

fs_server = MCPServerStdio(
    "npx",
    args=["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"],
)

sqlite_server = MCPServerStdio(
    "uvx",
    args=["mcp-server-sqlite", "--db-path", "/tmp/test.db"],
)

agent = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    mcp_servers=[fs_server, sqlite_server],
    system_prompt=(
        "You can read files via filesystem tools and run SQL via sqlite tools. "
        "When creating tables, use plain SQLite syntax."
    ),
)

async def main() -> None:
    with open("/tmp/hello.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write("Hello from MCP + Pydantic AI!")
    async with agent.run_mcp_servers():
        result = await agent.run(
            "Create a table called notes(content TEXT), "
            "insert the contents of /tmp/hello.txt into it, "
            "then SELECT it back and tell me what you read."
        )
        print(result.data)

asyncio.run(main())
```

Watch for tool-name collisions — both servers may expose tools like `list_resources`. If they do, prefix or only enable one at a time.
</details>
